description: Solo creator from Bishkek building an interactive 3D space adventure game for the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge. Players will explore Lunar and Martian landing sites, uncover real NASA mission stories behind discarded rovers and landers, and see their future legacy. Working solo on game design, storytelling, and NASA data integration. AI disclosure: Team avatar was generated with Claude, and this description was drafted with the help of Google Gemini.
summary:
"Relic Seekers" is an interactive, browser-based 3D space adventure game created for school-age space enthusiasts. Players become space archivists exploring authentic Lunar and Martian landing sites to locate discarded NASA hardware—including the Apollo 11 Eagle lander, the Lunar Laser Retroreflector, and the Opportunity rover.
Instead of reading static encyclopedia articles, students actively uncover space history by scanning artifacts, cleaning Martian dust off solar panels to unlock Opportunity’s final message, and completing interactive Cadet Quizzes. Completing the mission unlocks a "Year 2080: Lunar Heritage Dome" scene, demonstrating how preserving off-world monuments protects humanity’s scientific legacy and inspires future space explorers. Built with lightweight Three.js technology, the game runs smoothly on any smartphone or computer without downloads.
details:
What it does & How it works:

"Relic Seekers" is an interactive, browser-based 3D space adventure game created for the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge. Players step into the role of a space archivist traveling from an orbital Space Hub to authentic historical landing sites on the Moon (Sea of Tranquility) and Mars (Perseverance Valley). Using intuitive touch or desktop controls and floating waypoint markers, players explore low-gravity landscapes to locate discarded NASA hardware—including the Apollo 11 Eagle descent stage, the Lunar Laser Ranging Retroreflector, and the Opportunity rover. Scanning each relic reveals real scientific breakthroughs and triggers a 1-question interactive "Cadet Quiz." On Mars, players must actively clean dust off Opportunity’s solar panels to unlock its final telemetry message. Players can board their parked Explorer Shuttle to return to orbit, and scanning all relics unlocks a "Year 2080: Lunar Heritage Dome" scene showing how future generations preserve off-world monuments.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Designed specifically for school-age space enthusiasts, the game replaces passive reading with hands-on discovery. Its intended impact is to inspire young learners by reframing "abandoned" hardware not as space debris, but as living scientific heritage whose discoveries still benefit humanity today and guide future interplanetary exploration.

Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software Used:

The project was built as a lightweight, single-file web application using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and the open-source Three.js (WebGL) 3D graphics library, paired with procedural sound synthesis via the Web Audio API. Development and testing were completed across a smartphone and a standard computer using cloud-based AI coding assistants (Claude and Google Gemini) and GitHub Pages for public web hosting.

Creativity & Innovation:

Instead of creating a static webpage or slideshow, we blended low-poly 3D exploration with environmental storytelling and future-thinking perspective. Mechanics like physically wiping Martian dust off solar panels, boarding a return shuttle, and unlocking a futuristic 2080 lunar museum dome turn historical NASA archives into an emotional, memorable adventure.

Factors Considered:

Accessibility and hardware inclusivity were our top priorities. Knowing that many students and judges access projects from smartphones or older, low-end computers, we engineered a single-file, zero-download WebGL experience with low-poly optimization and custom dual controls (virtual on-screen joystick/buttons for mobile and keyboard/mouse support for desktop). We also carefully balanced scientific accuracy with simple, engaging language tailored to school-age players.
